image_description: A close-up, high-resolution photograph of a coral fungus (likely Ramaria or Clavulina species) growing on decaying wood. The fungus features a complex, multi-branched structure with a pale cream to light orange/pink coloration. The branches are thick at the base and divide into numerous finer, finger-like tips. The background consists of dark, textured bark and patches of green moss.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific taxonomic classification and rule out look-alike structures or AI hallucinations of fungal forms.
To verify that the intricate branching structure is topologically sound, with no fused branches or bleeding edges against the background moss/bark.
To assess the naturalness of the texture and lighting, ensuring the matte finish and organic irregularities are not artifacts of generation.
To ensure the depth relationship between the foreground fungus and the background wood/moss is physically consistent.

focus_areas: Branch connectivity and topology (no floating tips)
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the tips of the branches. AI generators often struggle with the termination of thin structures, causing them to melt into the background or end abruptly without natural tapering. Also, verify if the color gradient from the base to the tips is natural or if it shows banding/artificial smoothing.
